paper.title: Non-Stationary Representation Learning in Sequential Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential linear bandits sharing a single representation (within-environment)
unmapped: Multi-task: tau tasks played in sequence, each for N rounds (task change times known); task coefficients theta_i = B alpha_i share an unknown r-dimensional representation B
Action set is an ellipsoid {x: x^T M^{-1} x <= 1}
Task diversity assumption: every length-ell window has sigma_r(W W^T/ell) >= nu/r
Learner knows N, d, r and the order of ell; number of tasks tau unknown
Regret compares to per-task optimal action
settings.definition_quote: y_t= x_t^\top \theta_{q(t)} +\eta_t ... \CT= \{ \theta_1, \dots, \theta_\tau\}, where the number of tasks $\tau$ is unknown, and the representation shared by the tasks is $B \in \R^{d \times r}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-task sequential linear bandits in non-stationary environments
unmapped: S tasks each played N rounds (T = SN); tasks drawn from m environments in consecutive segments of unknown lengths tau_k; tasks in environment k lie in span of unknown r-dim representation B_k
Task diversity assumption with parameters ell, nu
Change-detection tuning uses kappa (min principal-angle sine between consecutive representations), theta_min, theta_max, nu, S
settings.definition_quote: the agent plays $S$ bandits in sequence and interacts with each bandit for $N$ rounds ... these tasks are drawn from $m$ different environments ... there exists a matrix $B_k\in \R^{d\times r_k}$ with orthonormal columns such that $\exists \alpha_i\in \R^{r_k}:\theta_i=B_k \alpha_i$

settings.name_in_paper: Single linear bandit task (ellipsoid action set)
unmapped: Action set is an ellipsoid; theta_min <= ||theta|| <= theta_max; horizon N
settings.definition_quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$, let the agent play it using RepE in Algorithm~\ref{alg:RE} for $N$ rounds.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde O \Big({d  r \sqrt{\tau N}}+ {\frac{d  r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+  \frac{d \ell}{r} \sqrt{\tau N } + \tau  r \sqrt{N} \Big)

symbols.tau: number of tasks in the sequence

source.label: regret:seq:single_B
source.quote: Let the agent play the series of bandits in Eq.~\eqref{Sequ_tasks} using SeqRepL in Algorithm~\ref{alg:SeqRepL}.  Select an $L$ such that $L =\Theta(\ell)$, and let $N_1=dr\sqrt{{N}/{L}}$ and $N_2=r\sqrt{N}$. Then, the regret $R_{\tau N}$ of SepRepL satisfies \BE [R_{\tau N}]= {\tilde O \Big({d  r \sqrt{\tau N}}+ ...+ \tau  r \sqrt{N} \Big)}.

results.notes: Total horizon tau*N. tau unknown to the algorithm so treated as anytime in number of tasks. Regret is pseudo-regret against per-task optimal action.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde O\left( d r \sqrt{\tau N}+ {\frac{d  r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+  \tau r \sqrt{N} \right)

source.label: Coro_seq
source.quote: Assume that $\ell$ in Assumption~\ref{Assump:diversity} is of the order of $r$, i.e., $\ell=\Theta(r^2)$. Let $N_1=d\sqrt{r N}$ and $N_2=r\sqrt{N}$. Then, the regret of SepRepL for the sequential bandits in Eq.~\eqref{Sequ_tasks} satisfies $\BE [R_{\tau N}]= \tilde O\left( d r \sqrt{\tau N}+ {\frac{d  r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+  \tau r \sqrt{N} \right)$.

results.notes: Statement inconsistently says 'order of r' and ell=Theta(r^2); recorded as Theta(r^2).

symbols.N_task: horizon N of the single task

source.label: regret:RepL
source.quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$,  let the agent play it using RepE in Algorithm~\ref{alg:RE} for $N$ rounds. Then, the regret $R_N$ of RepE satisfies $\BE [R_N] =  O(N_1+\frac{N}{N_1}d^2)$.

results.notes: Intermediate lemma; free exploration length N_1.

conditions: theta = B alpha for some r-dim orthonormal B
estimate hat B with ||hat B^T B_perp||_F <= varepsilon is given

source.label: transfer:single
source.quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$, assume that there exists $B\in \R^{d\times r}$ with orthonormal columns such that $\theta = B \alpha$ ... Assume that an estimate $\hat B$ is known and satisfies $\|\hat B^\top B_\perp\|_F  \le \varepsilon$. ... then the regret satisfies $\BE [R_N]= O( N_2+ \frac{N }{N_2}r^2+ N \varepsilon^2 ). $

bound.expression_latex: \tilde{O} \Big( \sum_{i=1}^{m} \big( {d  r \sqrt{\tau_i N}}+ { \frac{d  r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau_i N}}  +\frac{d \ell}{r} \sqrt{\tau_iN } \big) + S  r \sqrt{N} + S n_{\rm det}+ m b dr\sqrt{N\ell}  + 2m \Big)

symbols.tau_i: number of tasks in environment segment i
symbols.n_det: number of probing actions = ceil(9(d-r)log(2S^2N)/(theta_min^2 lambda_0^2 kappa^2))
symbols.b: number of initial exploration cycles (Eq. value:b)

tuning: n_det, xi_det as in Eq. det_selection:m

source.label: upp-bound:CD-RepL
source.quote: Let the agent play the sequential bandits in $\CS$ using the CD-RepL in Algorithm~\ref{alg:main}. Let $L=\Theta(\ell)$,  $n_{\rm det}$ and $\xi_{\rm det}$ be as in Eq.~\eqref{det_selection:m}, and $b$ be as in Eq.~\eqref{value:b}. Then, the regret of the CD-RepL satisfies \BE[R_{T}] = \tilde{O} \Big( \sum_{i=1}^{m} \big( ... \big) + S  r \sqrt{N} + S n_{\rm det}+ m b dr\sqrt{N\ell}  + 2m \Big).

results.notes: T = S N. n_det depends on kappa (min sine of principal angle between consecutive representations).

source.quote: Assume that $\ell=\Theta(r)$, $1/(\lambda_0^2 \nu^2)=\Theta(1)$, and  $\kappa$ satisfies \kappa \ge \max \big\{\min\{ p_1,p_2 \},\min \{p_3,p_4 \} \big\}, ... Then, the regret of CD-RepL for the sequential tasks in $\CS$ satisfies \BE [R_{SN}] = \tilde O \Big(\sum \nolimits _{i=1}^{m} {d r \sqrt{ \tau_i N}}+ S r \sqrt{N}  \Big).

results.notes: Text notes this is at most O~(d r sqrt(m S N) + S r sqrt(N)).

bound.expression_latex: \|\hat B^\top B_\perp\|_F \le \tilde O\left( \frac{d r}{\lambda_0 \nu}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{ nL N_1}}}  \right)

source.label: dist:B
source.quote: Then, for any cycle $n$, the estimate $\hat B$ at the end of the representation exploration phase satisfies \|\hat B^\top B_\perp\|_F \le \tilde O\left( \frac{d r}{\lambda_0 \nu}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{ nL N_1}}}  \right), with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{kN_1}$.

results.notes: Representation estimation error (subspace distance), not regret. Probability 1-1/(kN_1) with k = nL.
